submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the first token of a clause's verbal predicate: finite and light verbs ('keep', 'hold', 'led', 'shuttled', 'maintained', 'served'), copulas and auxiliaries ('is', 'are', 'been'), and the particle or preposition that completes a phrasal or reduced predicate ('to' after 'kept', 'on' after 'went', 'around' after 'been'), typically right after a subject, auxiliary, adverb or conjunction. It stays quiet on tokens that only extend an already-open noun phrase (nouns after determiners or numerals, punctuation, subword continuations); a weaker secondary trigger is the head word of a newly opened noun phrase such as a surname after a first name ('John K|rasinski').

rival_explanations: A generic word-onset detector: it fires on the first subword of almost any word that begins after whitespace, in any grammatical category, so its apparent preference for verbs and particles is only an artifact of which words happen to be token-initial or frequent, and it should fire just as strongly on determiners, nouns and fresh names.

A narrow lexical 'keep/be/have' neuron: it is tuned to copulas, auxiliaries and the keep/hold/maintain/shut/serve lemma family, so other predicate verbs (stay, find, continued, weakened) should drop the activation sharply rather than leaving it near its peak.
